newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened in a square position on Wednesday with short-term trading rates quoted unchanged from previous levels in quiet trade, dealers said.
"The market is quiet and rates are still firm. People are not trading much because they are waiting for tomorrow's (Thursday's weekly) Treasury Bill tender," a dealer said.
"No one is taking any long money at the moment because they can buy it cheaper on Thursday and Friday when we will have a lot of treasury bills maturing," he added.
Meanwhile on Wednesday, discount houses were indicating a steady selling rate of 19 percent for Treasury Bills.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were also unchanged at 24 percent (buying) and 20 percent (selling), and bankers acceptance bills also held to Tuesday's 22 and 19 percent. Call money was quoted at 24 percent.
